messages.subject: missing C function from affyPLM
parts:
Hi,
I am working on Exon Arrays. I have not used the 'fit' function since
last spring -- just been working off of my saved residuals and such --
but I now need to refit certain units because of the problems with the
cdf discussed earlier. When I run the fit function
(fit.ProbeLevelModel), I get an error that the basic function from
affyPLM is not found. Am I missing some sort of update, or is this an
specific problem for the exon array analysis that hasn't been caught
yet? (Running aroma.affymetrix v0.7.2, R 2.6.0)
Thanks,
Elizabeth

> fit(plmTissue,units=repUnits,force=T)
Error in .Call("R_rlm_rma_default_model", y, psiCode, psiK, PACKAGE =
"affyPLM") :
C symbol name "R_rlm_rma_default_model" not in DLL for package
"affyPLM"
> traceback()
8: .Call("R_rlm_rma_default_model", y, psiCode, psiK, PACKAGE =
"affyPLM")
7: fitfcn(y)
6: FUN(X[[1L]], ...)
5: base::lapply(unit, FUN = function(group) {
if (length(group) > 0) {
y <- .subset2(group, 1)
}
else {
y <- NULL
}
fitfcn(y)
})
4: FUN(X[[1L]], ...)
3: base::lapply(y, FUN = fitUnit)
2: fit.ProbeLevelModel(plmTissue, units = repUnits, force = T)
1: fit(plmTissue, units = repUnits, force = T)

messages.subject: Re: missing C function from affyPLM
parts:
Hi Ken and all,

So I have looked at Henrik's code for getFitFunction.RmaPlm. It has
changed substantially, and in particular, it has catches for
evaluating what is the version of affyPLM being used, and the newer
version calls from the 'preprocessCore' package. I wonder if it would
not be possible to use the 'RmaPlm' version of getFitFunction for the
exon array -- the main difference is calling median polish if there
are too many probesets per transcript cluster, right? Henrik has
different 'flavors' in getFitFunction.RmaPlm function (e.g. oglio) and
we could make an 'manyProbesets' flavor that would do a check on the
dimensions and then pick median polish or IWLS one? Or somehow make
Henrik's code about choosing the fitting function more modular so that
getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm can grab ahold of it? It just seems
pointless (and against the point of object oriented programming!) to
copy all the work Henrik does in keeping the getFitFunction up-to-
date. And clearly a recipe for disaster for mantaining the package.

I don't remember how much impact these two approaches would have (i.e.
how trickle down to other functions). What's your take on this, Ken?
(and Henrik, of course, when you get back, since either way requires a
change to your core code) Is it better to 1) make a 'flavor' within
getFitFunction.RmaPlm for the exon array fitting function and get rid
of getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm altogether or 2) cut out some of the
functions defined in getFitFunction.RmaPlm (e.g.
'getRlmPkg','rmaModelAffyPlmOld','rmaModelAffyPlm', etc.) and make
them globally available to be called appropriately (based on
dimension) by getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm? or 3) Both! make a large
number of probes 'flavor' (so get rid of ExonRmaPlm method) AND make
the functions more globally available. Henrik's code for the
getFitFunction.RmaPlm has additional advantages, in addition to
defining these functions -- validating that the answers make sense,
etc -- which we might as well not recreate either. Would there be some
interest by users in having the option to do median polish fitting
anyway for speed reasons? Perhaps it might be nice to make those
fitting functions somewhat globally available regardless (at a
developers level, not general users) if there are future uses of them
and then they only have to be mantained once.

In the meantime, I am going to patch in Henrik's code to update
getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm. When (if?) I get it working, I'll give it
to Henrik to make available as a patch.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: missing C function from affyPLM
parts:
I have rewritten the getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm so that it directly
calls getFitFunction.RmaPlm() to create a rma function and then uses
that function within a function that checks for the large number of
probes possible. Using it, the fit function now runs for me -- that's
about all the assurance I can give at this point! Henrik, I have
committed that function to the aroma.affymetrix.tools svn repository
if you want to make it available (under the 'R' folder, along with
other code that I have put there).

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Function available to correct fit function for Exon Arrays
parts:
Hi all,
I realized a patch for the problem with the exon arrays may not be
available soon. So if anyone is trying to run analysis on the exon
arrays, I have put a function on the group pages that (hopefully) fixes
the problems with fitting the probe level model for Exon Arrays. Please
let me know (via the group list) if there are problems with it, since I
haven't tested it on a fresh R session or anything.
http://aroma-affymetrix.googlegroups.com/web/getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm
Best,
Elizabeth

it's a petty I was away when you send your first message. Yes, the
problems you experienced are due to recent rearrangements in affyPLM
and preprocessCore. I though it was fixed in aroma.affymetrix v0.7.2
not only in the RmaPlm but also in the ExonRmaPlm class. When I look
at the v0.7.2 code of getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm() there is no
hardwired PACKAGE="affyPLM" but rather a PACKAGE=rlmPkg argument.
That is,

> digest2(getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm)
[1] "079f0e40517424e68e991024a135a3a6"
> print(getFitFunction.ExonRmaPlm)
function (this, ..., verbose = FALSE)
{
<snip>
fit <- .Call("R_rlm_rma_default_model", y, psiCode,
psiK, PACKAGE = rlmPkg)
<snip>
rlmPkg <- getRlmPkg(verbose = less(verbose))
verbose && cat(verbose, "rlmPkg: ", rlmPkg)
require(rlmPkg, character.only = TRUE) || throw("Package not loaded: ",
rlmPkg)
<snip>
rmaModel
}
attr(,"modifiers")

Don't you get the same?
